family.name: Equity Research Analyst
family.summary: A fast-growing listed company that looks cheap: find the red flags in its cash flow, receivables and promoter pledges, make a call, and fix a junior’s valuation built on a one-off gain.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What worries you?
stages.summary: Read four years of numbers: profits growing while cash flow vanishes, receivables doubling, rising related-party sales and pledges. Think aloud.

stages.title: Your recommendation
stages.summary: Make a call on a cheap stock with red flags. Think aloud.

stages.title: A month later
stages.summary: Events after their call. Tests updating views honestly.

stages.title: Check a junior's valuation
stages.summary: A valuation built on a one-off gain, a mismatched peer and ignored dilution. Think aloud.

stages.title: The investment note (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the summary note for the fund manager with AI. Catches hype and invented figures.

stages.title: A call you got wrong
stages.summary: A real investment or analytical call that went wrong. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're an equity research analyst covering **Kaveri Home Products**, a listed kitchen appliances maker. The stock trades at **15× earnings**, against 35× for its listed peers. Your fund manager asks for a recommendation by Friday.

items: In FY24 the statutory auditor resigned mid-term, citing "insufficient information to complete our review of certain transactions". A new auditor was appointed within a week.
Management on the last earnings call: "Best year in our history. Growth will continue at 25%."

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a time a number looked too good to be true.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What story do the numbers tell, and what worries you most?** Rank your concerns and say what each could mean.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Buy: the growth is real and the stock is cheap
Sell or avoid: the cash flow and governance signs are too serious
No rating until you have spoken to management

prompt.text: **What do you recommend to the fund manager?** Pick one, give your reasons, and say what would make you change your mind.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Buy: the growth is real and the stock is cheap"

prompt.text: The stock rose 15%, then the new auditor qualified the accounts over related-party receivables. It fell 22% in a day. The fund manager asks what you missed.
**What do you say and do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Hold: good growth, some questions"

prompt.text: On a management call, the CFO says the receivables are from "a new distributor channel with longer credit terms". You find the largest new distributor is owned by the promoter's brother-in-law.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Sell or avoid: the cash flow and governance signs are too serious"

prompt.text: The company reported a strong quarter and the stock rose 24%. A client tells the fund manager your call "cost them money", and another analyst publishes a Buy.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "No rating until you have spoken to management"

prompt.text: Management agreed to a call, then cancelled twice. They won't share the receivables ageing. The fund manager needs your view by tomorrow.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A junior analyst drafted this valuation. **Find the problems, worst first, and say which way each one pushes the target price.**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: FY24 earnings used as the base, including a 28 (₹ crore) gain from selling a factory plot.
Target multiple: average of three peers, one of which is a much larger, debt-free consumer goods leader at 59× earnings.
Share count: current shares only. (The promoter holds warrants that convert into 8% more shares next year.)
Revenue forecasts: in line with the consensus of other analysts.
Conclusion: 60% upside. Strong Buy.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the summary of your investment note for the fund manager (under 180 words): your call, the three reasons, and the risks to your view.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about an investment or analysis call you got wrong.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
